      "content": "# @indexyz/dsh-autocompact

Set an earlier automatic compaction threshold per model, or for every model at once, on
the [dsh (DeepSeek Harness)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) coding
agent. This is the dsh port of [`@indexyz/pi-autocompact`](https://github.com/5aaee9/pi-agent-extensions/tree/main/pi-autocompact).

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @indexyz/dsh-autocompact
```

To install a repository checkout, run from the repository root:

```bash
npm install
npm run build --workspace @indexyz/dsh-autocompact
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-autocompact
```

Build output is Git-ignored. Local `link:` installs read that output directly;
`npm pack` builds it automatically before creating a published package.

It is built and tested against dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` and declares that range as
`engines.dsh` (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`), which the plugin market reads before it
installs: on a harness outside it the market refuses the install instead of
installing something that breaks. Node `22.19.0` or newer is required as well.

```text
/autocompact 300k    # 300,000 tokens, current session/model only
/autocompact 0.3m    # same threshold; k/m are decimal units
/autocompact 300000
/autocompact         # show current threshold and native enabled state
/autocompact off     # use the backend defaults, ignoring global plugin defaults in this session
/autocompact default # clear the session override and inherit the global default
```

Commands never write configuration, append threshold entries to the session log,
reload plugins, or modify the model's real context-window metadata. Overrides are
keyed by exact `provider/model`. Switching models preserves each model's session
override; new, resumed, and forked sessions start clean. `off` does not disable
the backend's own automatic compaction or overflow recovery.

The effective threshold for a route is resolved in this order: the session's
`/autocompact` override (an explicit `off` suppresses everything below it), the
route's own entry in `modelLimits`, then the deployment-wide `defaultLimit`. A
route with none of these keeps the backend's own automatic compaction.

## Settings page

**Settings → Autocompact** manages the persisted deployment defaults that every
session inherits, so a threshold can be set without editing YAML:

- a master switch for all configured thresholds;
- a **Default threshold** applied to every model that has no threshold of its own,
  left blank to keep those models on the backend's compaction;
- one row per exact `provider/model` route with its threshold in tokens, editable
  in place and removable;
- an add-model control fed by the live model catalog, with a manual
  `provider/model` field when the catalog is unavailable.

The composer's status pill opens this section (see below); the same editor is also
registered as a central panel, which is the pill's fallback destination when the
settings shell's store cannot be reached.

The page writes the bundle row's `modelLimits` and `defaultLimit` through the Host
`settings` service, guarded by the row's revision and validated by its Config schema,
so values land in the profile patch layer and survive upgrades. `writable: false`
profiles render the page read-only. `modelLimits`, `defaultLimit`, and `enabled` are
declared `.volatile()`: the settings service lists only entries whose Config has a
volatile field and accepts writes only to volatile paths, and a volatile field is
what makes a saved edit reach the running plugin without a restart. `retainTokens`
stays ordinary configuration and is edited in YAML only.

The client half reaches that namespace as its own Cordis service
(`remote.settings`, declared in `inject`) rather than as a property of the
`remote` service: Cordis resolves a nested service only for a context that
declares it, and reading it otherwise throws. The model catalog is read
opportunistically from `remote.session`, so a deployment without it still gets
the manual route field. The section also carries its own error boundary, so a
crash shows its message and stack in place instead of leaving an empty page.

The page's type scale and controls are settings-page values, copied from the
shipped packages rather than chosen here: the 18/600 page title and 13px intro of
`dsh-client-ui-agent-preset`, a 12/18 hint and 14/22 row label from
`dsh-client-ui-settings-models` (the same management-list shape this page has) and
`dsh-client-ui-settings-account`, the 32px field from the primitives'
`Input.module.css`, the 36px button with its 28px row variant and the card tokens
from the settings pages, and the 36x20 switch from `Switch.module.css`. The host's
sections are not uniform — Models, Account and Shortcuts declare a 16/500/24 page
title, Agent presets an 18/600 one — so this takes the heavier of the two, which is
the section adjacent to this one. Tokens the Theme provider does not document
(`label-tertiary`, `border-l3`, `settings-card-*`, `button-primary-*`, the radii)
are used with the documented token as a fallback, so a rename degrades the
appearance instead of erasing it.

## Composer status line

A compact status entry sits in the composer's ambient row
(`conversation.composer.dock`), right beside the session's turn, token, and
context readings, so the state is visible without opening Settings:

| It shows             | When                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `(icon) 128K / 300K` | a threshold applies to this session's model (its own entry or the deployment default): the first figure is the measured pressure from `contextPressure`, the second the threshold that triggers compaction |
| `(icon) 300K`        | a threshold applies, but no request has reported usage yet                                                                                                                                                 |
| `(icon) Off`         | the master switch is off                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| nothing              | neither a model threshold nor a deployment default applies, or the deployment exposes no configurable autocompact row                                                                                      |

The pill is dressed as one of the host's own ambient readings: the icon artwork (the host's data-outline icon),
the pill padding, radius and tertiary label colour, the density-aware type size,
and the `{value}K`/`{value}M` count units all match the composer's own stats and
context readings, so nothing about it stands out. It carries no word of the
plugin's own name — the icon identifies the entry, and the tooltip (`title` and
`aria-label`) stays two short lines: the route and what the number means, then
what a click does (`deepseek/x: 128K of 300K` / `Click to open settings`).

It takes a seat in that row only when it has something to report: a model
without a threshold of its own and no deployment default under an on switch is a
non-event, and the Settings page is where "not configured" is discovered and
fixed — so an inert autocompact does not add noise to the session's own readings.

Clicking the pill opens **Settings → Autocompact**. Settings owns the panel, its
section navigation, and the store behind both, and the shell registers that store
with a handle pinned to the live instance — `{ ...handle, create: () => instance }`
— so resolving the seat through the slot registry answers the very store the panel
renders from, and the shell's own `openSection(id)` (documented on its owner props
as "open the settings panel directly on one registered section") selects this
plugin's section and opens the modal. The lookup goes by capability, not by
position: only a store whose action table carries `openSection` is asked, because a
store declared any other way mints a fresh, unsubscribed instance whose actions
change nothing on screen.

As a fallback, this plugin also registers a central panel under its own key that
renders the same editor component from the same store as the Settings section, and
the pill selects it through the `layout` service when the settings shell's store
cannot be reached (a renamed cell or action, or a profile without settings). `selectPanel`
throws for an unregistered key, so both paths are guarded; in a composition with
neither, the click is inert and the reading still renders.

It reads the session's route from the `modelSelection` projection and subscribes
to the same configuration store the Settings page writes to, so a save there
updates the line immediately. The configured number is the **deployment
default** for the route, falling back to the deployment-wide default:
`/autocompact` overrides live in Host memory for one session and are not
published to the client, so the pill shows the persisted threshold and does not
claim to be the effective value — a session override is not visible here.
A crash inside the pill is caught by its own boundary, which logs and renders
nothing, because the composer must survive a decorative widget.

## How it works on dsh

`dsh-compaction-basic` already condenses history as token pressure builds, using
`floor(min(W × thresholdRatio, W − reservedOutput − headroomTokens))`. This plugin
adds only one thing: an **earlier absolute threshold**, per model or for every
model, for the current session, expressed through the public compaction seam.

- On every `agent/pre-step` boundary the plugin measures request pressure with
  `ctx.tokenMeter` and compares it with the effective threshold. Above it, the
  plugin selects a balanced surface range that keeps the backend's own
  `retainTokens`/`retainRatio` recent tail verbatim, then calls
  `compactRegion(start, end, agent, signal)` on the session's backend. The backend
  writes the summary and the ordinary `compaction/*` records; the turn continues
  with normal tool and follow-up scheduling. No synthetic prompt is injected and
  the run is never aborted.
- Because a new prompt enters through the same `agent/pre-step` boundary, a large
  existing session is also compacted before its next request — the dsh equivalent
  of Pi's idle-input path, without a second code path.
- Failures are contained and reported once per session: a failed summary leaves
  context intact and the next step can try again.

### Where the backend comes from

The shipped Web bundle disables the Host-plane `compaction-basic` row and lets
each Agent preset mount its own instance inside an `isolate` realm. A single Host
row therefore cannot `inject` `compaction`; this plugin mounts on the Host plane
(one row serves every preset) and addresses the backend of the exact Agent at
event time:

1. `serviceForAgent(ctx, agent, "compaction")` from
   `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry` — the preset-mounted instance.
2. `ctx.get("compaction")` — the Host-plane instance, for compositions such as
   the headless, ACP, and SDK bundles that mount it there.

Overrides stay keyed by session and route, so they follow the Agent, not the
preset revision.

## Optional global defaults

Persist defaults in the bundle row's `config` (profile `cordis.patch.yml`), not in
the command:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: autocompact
      name: "@indexyz/dsh-autocompact"
      config:
        defaultLimit: 300000
        modelLimits:
          provider/model-id: 400000
```

| Field          | Default | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `modelLimits`  | `{}`    | Global default thresholds keyed by exact `provider/model`; positive integer token counts.                               |
| `defaultLimit` | unset   | Threshold applied to every model without a `modelLimits` entry; unset means those models keep the backend's compaction. |
| `retainTokens` | `20000` | Recent-tail fallback budget, used only when the mounted backend publishes no retention policy.                          |
| `enabled`      | `true`  | Master switch for the automatic pressure check.                                                                         |

Values are positive integer token counts. A `modelLimits` entry overrides
`defaultLimit`, and a session command overrides both without changing the row
configuration. The Settings page above writes `modelLimits`, `defaultLimit`, and
`enabled`, so YAML and UI stay interchangeable; clearing the default in the page
(or deleting the key in YAML) turns autocompact off for uncovered models again.

## Behavior and limitations

- The mounted backend must support explicit region compaction
  (`compactRegion` on the backend, shipped by `dsh-compaction` 0.2.0-rc.2 and
  newer). Otherwise the command reports the missing capability and the hook is
  inert.
- A backend that publishes `config.auto === false` disables automatic compaction;
  the plugin respects that and refuses to set a threshold.
- Retention follows the backend's own policy for the exact route, so the
  threshold must exceed the retained tail and stay below the real model context
  window. Both are validated before a threshold is accepted.
- A deployment-wide `defaultLimit` is validated once at load as a positive token
  count, then checked against each route's real capacity when that route is used.
  A default that does not fit one model's context window leaves that model
  uncompacted and warns once per session; other routes keep using it.
- Thresholds are not strict request-size caps: one turn or tool batch can
  overshoot. If an indivisible or too-small context cannot retain recent content
  and shrink, the plugin leaves it to the backend's overflow or manual
  compaction.
- The backend's automatic threshold is untouched, so a plugin threshold above it
  never delays compaction.
- Summary generation consumes model tokens. Failures leave context intact and are
  not retried at the same boundary; a subsequent step can try again.

## Development

Both halves are TypeScript; only their build targets differ.

```bash
npm run check          # typecheck, build both halves, then test
npm run build          # lib/ (Host, tsc) + client.js (browser half, tsdown)
npm run build:host     # Host half only: index.ts/settings.ts/compaction.ts -> lib/
npm run build:client   # browser half only: src/client/index.tsx -> client.js
```

The Host half compiles to `lib/` with `tsc`. The browser half is authored under
`src/client/` and built by [tsdown](https://tsdown.dev) (oxc/rolldown) into the
Git-ignored `client.js`: that is the artifact `exports["./client"]` publishes and
the Harness page loads, so it must be one
`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` registration. The build supplies
that wrapper and leaves `react` / `react/jsx-runtime` external, because the
page's module table provides them — edit the source, then run
`npm run build:client` (the artifact carries a generated-file header, and the
workspace formatter and linter skip it).

| File                                  | Role                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `index.tsx`                           | `inject` + `apply`: the registration the loader materializes             |
| `contracts.ts`                        | the Host, locale, slot, and Remote-namespace shapes this half depends on |
| `services.ts`                         | access to those services (`remote.settings`, `remote.session`)           |
| `state.ts`                            | the page's state shapes and the pure derivations over them               |
| `limits.ts`                           | the `300k` threshold grammar and count formatting                        |
| `dictionary.ts`, `styles.ts`          | this half's localized strings and section styles                         |
| `page.tsx`                            | the section: its state, Host reads/writes, and layout                    |
| `threshold-list.tsx`, `add-model.tsx` | the two editable views the page renders                                  |
| `crash-boundary.tsx`                  | the section's own crash face                                             |

      "content": "# pi-agent-extensions

A collection of extensions for the [pi coding agent](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono), and for the [dsh (DeepSeek Harness)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) coding agent.

## Packages

| Package                                                                                     | Description                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`@indexyz/pi-provider-sub2api`](./pi-provider-sub2api)                                     | Dynamic provider support, model metadata discovery, quota reporting, saved request modes, and Grok (xAI) entries for Sub2API-compatible relays. |
| [`@indexyz/pi-custom-provider`](./pi-custom-provider)                                       | Generic OpenAI Chat Compatible, Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses, and Ollama providers with model discovery and caching.                    |
| [`@indexyz/pi-continue`](./pi-continue)                                                     | Resume an interrupted or failed turn with pi's currently selected model.                                                                        |
| [`@indexyz/pi-skill`](./pi-skill)                                                           | Codex-style `$skill-name` invocation anywhere in a prompt.                                                                                      |
| [`@indexyz/pi-model-trace`](./pi-model-trace)                                               | Attribute the model actually serving pi via ModelTrace numeric fingerprinting (`/model-trace`).                                                 |
| [`@indexyz/pi-autocompact`](./pi-autocompact)                                               | Session-only per-model context compaction thresholds via `/autocompact 300k`, with optional global defaults.                                    |
| [`@indexyz/dsh-autocompact`](./dsh-autocompact)                                             | The same thresholds for dsh: a `/autocompact` command, a Settings section, and a composer status entry.                                         |
| [`@indexyz/dsh-custom-provider-reasoning-efforts`](./dsh-custom-provider-reasoning-efforts) | Declare `reasoningEfforts` and `input` modalities for hand-written dsh provider routes the pi-ai catalog does not describe.                     |
| [`@indexyz/dsh-thread-summary`](./dsh-thread-summary)                                       | Generate a concise session title from the first user prompt with a configurable summary model.                                                  |
| [`@indexyz/dsh-prompt-suggestions`](./dsh-prompt-suggestions)                               | Suggest the user's next message as dim ghost text in an empty composer after a successful reply.                                                |

Install a package from npm:

```bash
pi install npm:@indexyz/pi-provider-sub2api
pi install npm:@indexyz/pi-custom-provider
pi install npm:@indexyz/pi-continue
pi install npm:@indexyz/pi-skill
pi install npm:@indexyz/pi-model-trace
pi install npm:@indexyz/pi-autocompact
```

A `dsh-<topic>/` package is installed into a dsh profile instead, and its command line, configuration, and behavior are documented in its own README:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @indexyz/dsh-autocompact
dsh plugin --profile web add @indexyz/dsh-thread-summary
dsh plugin --profile web add @indexyz/dsh-prompt-suggestions
```

## Releases

Each package is versioned and released independently. A release of one package publishes only that package, and each published version is tagged `@indexyz/<name>@<version>` (for example `@indexyz/pi-skill@0.1.43`) with a GitHub Release carrying that version's changelog section. Every package's history is in its own `CHANGELOG.md`. The release procedure is [`docs/releases.md`](./docs/releases.md).

Every new npm package starts with an independent empty `0.0.0` workspace: the owner publishes it with the `bootstrap` tag and configures npm Trusted Publisher before the formal version is pushed to GitHub for CI publication. Follow [First release of a new package](./docs/releases.md#first-release-of-a-new-package) for the workspace template, commands and publisher settings.

## Layout

The repository root is a private npm workspace that holds shared tooling and documentation only. Each package lives in its own root-level directory with its own `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, tests, and changelog: `pi-<topic>/` for a pi extension, `dsh-<topic>/` for a dsh package, which builds its own artifacts from TypeScript because the Harness loads built files rather than sources. See [`docs/architecture.md`](./docs/architecture.md).

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run format
npm run check
pi -e ./pi-provider-sub2api/index.ts
```

`npm run check` runs the format check, lint, every package's typecheck, the build step of every package that declares one, every package's tests, and the release-script tests. Try a pi package from a checkout with `pi -e ./<name>/index.ts`.

Dsh build output (`lib/` and optional `client.js`) is Git-ignored; `npm pack` builds and includes it automatically. Before installing a dsh checkout into a profile, run `npm run build --workspace @indexyz/<name>`, then `dsh plugin --profile web add ./<name>`.

OpenSpec is installed with the repository tooling. Run `npx openspec <command>` from the repository root for shared changes, or from a package directory for changes to that package.

Contributors and coding agents start with [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md), which links the rest of [`docs/`](./docs).

      "content": "/**
 * Session-only per-model automatic compaction thresholds for dsh.
 *
 * The dsh port of `@indexyz/pi-autocompact`. A `/autocompact 300k` threshold is
 * kept in memory for the current session and model only; when the measured
 * request pressure crosses it, the plugin compacts an explicit balanced surface
 * range through the session's mounted compaction backend before the next
 * request. Nothing is written to configuration, the session log carries only
 * the backend's ordinary compaction records, and the model's real context-window
 * metadata is never modified.
 *
 * `compaction` is not a Host-plane service: the shipped Web bundle disables the
 * root row and lets each Agent preset mount its own isolated instance. This
 * plugin therefore mounts on the Host plane (so one row serves every preset) and
 * addresses the backend of the exact Agent at event time through
 * {@link serviceForAgent}, falling back to the Host plane for compositions (the
 * headless, ACP, and SDK bundles) that do mount it there.
 *
 * @module @indexyz/dsh-autocompact
 */
import z from "@deepseek-ai/schemastery";
import { serviceForAgent } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry";
import { CommandDefinitionId } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-commands/brand";
import type { Context } from "@deepseek-ai/cordis";
import type { Agent } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent";
import type { CompactionEngine } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction";
import type { CommandInvocation, CommandResult } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-commands";
import type { Session } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-session";
import { needsCompaction, selectCompactableRange } from "./compaction.ts";
import {
  defaultLimits,
  modelKey,
  nativeAutoEnabled,
  nativePolicy,
  nativeRetainTokens,
  parseLimit,
  resolveLimit,
  supportsRegions,
  validateDefaultLimit,
  validateLimit,
} from "./settings.ts";

/** Plugin identity used by the Loader and by diagnostics. */
export const name = "autocompact";

/** Host-plane services this plugin needs before it can register its command and hook. */
export const inject = ["commands", "tokenMeter", "llm"];

/** A `.volatile()` Config field: the Loader parses it into a stable reference read with `get()`. */
export interface VolatileField<T> {
  get(): T | undefined;
}

/**
 * Row configuration as `apply` receives it.
 *
 * The two fields the Settings page writes are declared `.volatile()`, so the
 * Loader hands `apply` live references rather than plain values; a direct call
 * (tests, embedding) may still pass plain values.
 */
export interface AutocompactConfig {
  /** Optional global default thresholds keyed by exact `provider/model`. Never written by the command. */
  modelLimits?: Record<string, number> | VolatileField<Record<string, number>>;
  /**
   * Optional deployment-wide threshold applied to every model without its own
   * entry. Absent means those models keep the backend's automatic compaction.
   */
  defaultLimit?: number | VolatileField<number | undefined>;
  /** Recent-tail fallback budget used only when the backend publishes no retention policy. */
  retainTokens?: number;
  /** Master switch for the automatic pressure check. */
  enabled?: boolean | VolatileField<boolean>;
}

/**
 * Validated row configuration; misconfiguration fails plugin load.
 *
 * `modelLimits`, `defaultLimit` and `enabled` are volatile because the Settings
 * page edits them through the Host settings service: that service only exposes
 * an entry whose schema declares a volatile field (`volatileForm`), and only
 * accepts writes to volatile paths. A volatile field is also what makes an edit
 * visible to the running plugin without a restart. `retainTokens` stays ordinary
 * configuration, editable from `cordis.patch.yml` only.
 */
export const Config = z.object({
  modelLimits: z.dict(z.natural()).default({}).volatile(),
  defaultLimit: z.natural().volatile(),
  retainTokens: z.natural().default(20000),
  enabled: z.boolean().default(true).volatile(),
});

interface Target {
  readonly provider: string;
  readonly model: string;
}

/**
 * Read one Config field, whether the Loader handed over a volatile reference or
 * a plain value, and re-read it on every call so a live Settings write is
 * visible to the running plugin.
 *
 * @param field - the parsed field, a volatile reference, or `undefined`.
 * @param fallback - value used when the field is absent or its reference is empty.
 * @returns the current plain value.
 */
function liveValue<T>(field: T | VolatileField<T> | undefined, fallback: T): T {
  if (field === undefined) return fallback;
  if (typeof field === "object" && field !== null) {
    const reference = field as VolatileField<T>;
    if (typeof reference.get === "function") return reference.get() ?? fallback;
  }
  return field as T;
}

interface SessionState {
  readonly overrides: Map<string, number | null>;
  readonly warned: Set<string>;
}

interface RouteInfo {
  readonly target: Target;
  readonly key: string;
  readonly contextWindow: number | undefined;
  readonly retainTokens: number;
}

/** Resolve the exact routed route for one agent, mirroring the backend's own lookup. */
export function targetOf(agent: Agent): Target | undefined {
  const header = agent.session.requestHeader()?.config;
  if (header !== undefined && header.provider.length > 0 && header.model.length > 0) {
    return { provider: header.provider, model: header.model };
  }
  const options = agent.options;
  if (
    typeof options?.provider === "string" &&
    options.provider.length > 0 &&
    typeof options.model === "string" &&
    options.model.length > 0
  ) {
    return { provider: options.provider, model: options.model };
  }
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * Resolve the compaction backend serving one Agent.
 *
 * A preset-mounted backend is isolated to that Agent's preset realm, so the
 * Agent's own identity is the only key that reaches it; compositions that mount
 * a backend on the Host plane are served by the direct lookup instead.
 *
 * @param ctx - this plugin's Host-plane context.
 * @param agent - the Agent whose backend is requested.
 * @returns the backend, or `undefined` when this composition mounts none.
 */
export function backendFor(ctx: Context, agent: Agent): CompactionEngine | undefined {
  try {
    const mounted = serviceForAgent(ctx, agent, "compaction");
    if (mounted !== undefined) return mounted;
  } catch {
    // A torn-down scope or an absent preset runtime leaves only the Host plane.
  }
  return ctx.get("compaction");
}

/**
 * Register the session-only `/autocompact` command and the automatic pressure
 * check for every Agent.
 *
 * @param ctx - Host-plane context carrying the command registry, the token meter, and the LLM registry.
 * @param config - validated row configuration; the Settings-editable fields arrive as live references.
 */
export function apply(ctx: Context, config: AutocompactConfig = {}): void {
  /** Current global defaults, re-read so a Settings write applies to the running plugin. */
  const limitsNow = (): Map<string, number> =>
    defaultLimits({ modelLimits: liveValue(config.modelLimits, {}) });
  /**
   * Current deployment-wide threshold, re-read like the defaults above.
   * `undefined` means no default: uncovered models keep the backend's behavior.
   */
  const defaultLimitNow = (): number | undefined =>
    validateDefaultLimit(liveValue<number | undefined>(config.defaultLimit, undefined));
  const fallbackRetainTokens = liveValue(config.retainTokens, 20000);
  // Validate the configured defaults at load, where a bad row fails loudly,
  // instead of at the first measured step.
  limitsNow();
  defaultLimitNow();
  // Session-only state, keyed by the live Session object so a new, resumed, or
  // forked session starts clean and a detached session is collected.
  const sessions = new WeakMap<Session, SessionState>();

  const stateOf = (session: Session): SessionState => {
    let state = sessions.get(session);
    if (state === undefined) {
      state = { overrides: new Map(), warned: new Set() };
      sessions.set(session, state);
    }
    return state;
  };

  const warnOnce = (session: Session, message: string): void => {
    const { warned } = stateOf(session);
    if (warned.has(message)) return;
    warned.add(message);
    ctx.logger.warn(`autocompact: ${message}`);
  };

  /** Resolve the exact route, its real window, and the backend's retained-tail budget. */
  const routeInfo = async (
    agent: Agent,
    backend: CompactionEngine,
    signal?: AbortSignal,
  ): Promise<RouteInfo | undefined> => {
    const target = targetOf(agent);
    if (target === undefined) return undefined;
    const info = await ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo(target.provider, target.model, signal);
    const contextWindow = info.context?.contextWindow;
    const reserved = agent.session.requestHeader()?.config.maxTokens ?? info.defaultMaxTokens ?? 0;
    return {
      target,
      key: modelKey(target.provider, target.model),
      contextWindow,
      retainTokens:
        contextWindow === undefined
          ? fallbackRetainTokens
          : nativeRetainTokens(
              nativePolicy(backend),
              target.provider,
              target.model,
              contextWindow,
              reserved,
              fallbackRetainTokens,
            ),
    };
  };

  /**
   * Compact an explicit balanced range once the session crosses its effective
   * threshold. Failures are contained: the turn continues untouched, exactly
   * like the backend's own automatic pressure path.
   */
  const checkPressure = async (agent: Agent, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<void> => {
    if (!liveValue(config.enabled, true) || signal.aborted) return;
    const target = targetOf(agent);
    if (target === undefined) return;
    const key = modelKey(target.provider, target.model);
    const limit = resolveLimit(
      stateOf(agent.session).overrides,
      limitsNow(),
      key,
      defaultLimitNow(),
    );
    if (limit === undefined) return;
    const backend = backendFor(ctx, agent);
    if (backend === undefined || !nativeAutoEnabled(backend)) return;
    const measurement = ctx.tokenMeter.measure(agent.session);
    if (!needsCompaction(measurement, limit)) return;
    if (!supportsRegions(backend)) {
      warnOnce(
        agent.session,
        "the mounted compaction backend does not support compactRegion; thresholds have no effect",
      );
      return;
    }
    const route = await routeInfo(agent, backend, signal);
    if (route === undefined || route.contextWindow === undefined) {
      warnOnce(
        agent.session,
        `no context capacity for ${key}; configure contextWindow on that adapter model`,
      );
      return;
    }
    if (signal.aborted) return;
    validateLimit(limit, route.contextWindow, route.retainTokens);
    const range = selectCompactableRange(agent.session, measurement, route.retainTokens);
    if (range === undefined) return;
    ctx.logger.info(
      `autocompact: compacting ${key} above ${limit.toLocaleString("en-US")} tokens (${measurement.totalTokens.toLocaleString("en-US")} measured)`,
    );
    await backend.compactRegion(range.start, range.end, agent, signal);
  };

  ctx.on("agent/pre-step", async ({ agent, signal }, next) => {
    try {
      await checkPressure(agent, signal);
    } catch (error) {
      if (!signal.aborted) {
        warnOnce(
          agent.session,
          `compaction failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
        );
      }
    }
    return next();
  });

  const handler = async (invocation: CommandInvocation): Promise<CommandResult> => {
    const { agent, rawInput, signal } = invocation;
    try {
      const target = targetOf(agent);
      if (target === undefined) return { kind: "error", text: "No model selected" };
      const key = modelKey(target.provider, target.model);
      const backend = backendFor(ctx, agent);
      if (backend === undefined) {
        return { kind: "error", text: `No compaction backend is mounted for ${key}` };
      }
      if (!supportsRegions(backend)) {
        return {
          kind: "error",
          text: "Autocompact requires a compaction backend that supports compactRegion (dsh-compaction 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer)",
        };
      }
      const nativeOff = !nativeAutoEnabled(backend);
      const route = await routeInfo(agent, backend, signal);
      if (route === undefined || route.contextWindow === undefined) {
        return {
          kind: "error",
          text: `No context capacity for ${key}; configure contextWindow on that adapter model`,
        };
      }
      const input = rawInput.trim().toLowerCase();
      const state = stateOf(agent.session).overrides;
      if (input === "off") state.set(key, null);
      else if (input === "default") state.delete(key);
      else if (input) {
        const limit = parseLimit(input);
        validateLimit(limit, route.contextWindow, route.retainTokens);
        if (nativeOff) {
          return {
            kind: "error",
            text: "Automatic compaction is disabled by the compaction backend. Enable it before setting a threshold.",
          };
        }
        state.set(key, limit);
      }
      const defaults = limitsNow();
      const limit = resolveLimit(state, defaults, key, defaultLimitNow());
      // Name the layer the effective threshold came from: the session, an exact
      // `provider/model` default, or the deployment-wide fallback.
      const source = state.has(key)
        ? "session"
        : defaults.has(key)
          ? "global default"
          : "deployment default";
      const threshold =
        limit === undefined
          ? "backend default compaction (no plugin threshold)"
          : `autocompact above ${limit.toLocaleString("en-US")} tokens (${source})`;
      return {
        kind: "success",
        text: `${key}: ${threshold}. Native automatic compaction: ${nativeOff ? "disabled" : "enabled"}. No configuration written.`,
      };
    } catch (error) {
      return { kind: "error", text: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) };
    }
  };

  ctx.effect(
    () =>
      ctx.commands.register({
        definitionId: CommandDefinitionId("@indexyz/dsh-autocompact"),
        name: "autocompact",
        description:
          "Session-only per-model compaction threshold: /autocompact [300k | off | default]",
        input: { hint: "300k | off | default" },
        handler,
      }),
    "dsh-autocompact command",
  );
}

      "content": "/**
 * Surface range selection for an earlier, session-only compaction threshold.
 *
 * This is the dsh translation of `pi-autocompact`'s `planCompaction`: instead of
 * planning over Pi's projected boundary context, it selects an inclusive
 * positional range on the dsh session surface, keeping the priced recent tail
 * verbatim and never splitting one step's assistant tool-call from its result.
 *
 * @module @indexyz/dsh-autocompact/compaction
 */
import { toolPairingBalancedBefore } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction";
import type { Session, SessionSeq } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-session";
import type { TokenMeasurement } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter";

/** One inclusive positional span on the session surface. */
export interface CompactableRange {
  /** First surface-node seq to replace, inclusive. */
  readonly start: SessionSeq;
  /** Last surface-node seq to replace, inclusive. */
  readonly end: SessionSeq;
}

/**
 * Whether the measured request pressure already crossed the effective absolute
 * threshold. Unknown or absent usage is never above it.
 */
export function needsCompaction(
  measurement: Pick<TokenMeasurement, "totalTokens">,
  limit: number,
): boolean {
  const tokens = measurement.totalTokens;
  return typeof tokens === "number" && tokens > limit;
}

/** The `system/message` occupying surface node 0, or `undefined` for other heads. */
export function systemHead(session: Session, headSeq: SessionSeq) {
  const head = session.eventAt(headSeq);
  return head?.type === "system/message" ? head : undefined;
}

/**

 * `k`/`m` are decimal units, matching the reference extension.

export function parseLimit(input: string): number {

  if (!match) throw new Error("Usage: /autocompact [300k | 1m | 300000 | off | default]");

    throw new Error("Threshold must be a positive safe integer number of tokens");
  }

 * backend will keep verbatim and against the real model context window.

  defaults: ReadonlyMap<string, number>,

        limit: threshold,
        tokens: formatTokens(now),
        action: t("dockAction"),
      })}
      text={`${formatTokens(now)} / ${threshold}`}
    />
  );
